field.label: Device, alias or port
field.help: A MAC address keeps working when the device gets a new address (ex. aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff); note that containers on ipvlan share their host's MAC, so they all get its priority. An IP address or network (ex. 192.168.1.20 or 192.168.1.32/28), or the name of a host or network alias (ex. work_laptops), also work. A protocol and port (range) marks that traffic from every device, in both directions (ex. udp/51820 for a WireGuard tunnel, tcp+udp/6881-6889 for a file-sharing port).

field.label: Priority
field.help: Interactive: CAKE's Video class, low delay with priority up to half the line, after that it shares like everyone else (ex. video calls, games). Background: CAKE's Bulk class, it gives way to everything else when the line is full (ex. backups, game downloads). Neither reserves bandwidth: unused capacity is always shared.

field.label: Description
field.help: Ex. "Living-room console". Shown in this list only.
